title: Stretch: Biopolymers and Sustainable Polymer Choices
welcome_lead: Look past oil-based plastics into PLA, bio-based polymers and the ethics of polymer use.
meta_desc: Stretch into biopolymers, additives and sustainable polymer strategies.
final_note: You can balance environmental, performance and cost factors when picking a polymer.

concepts.def: Polymer made from renewable plant sources.
Polylactic acid biopolymer from corn starch.
Breaks down to soil under composting conditions.
Additive that makes a polymer more flexible.
Colour additive mixed into polymer melt.
Additive that resists heat or UV damage.

walkthroughs.body_html: PLA is made from fermented corn starch and is used for 3D printing filament and food packaging. It is compostable in industrial facilities but can persist in normal landfills, so disposal route matters as much as the source.

Raw polymers are often modified. Plasticisers soften PVC for cable insulation, pigments give colour without painting, and stabilisers stop UV damage in outdoor products. Additives can complicate recycling, so designers must plan end-of-life carefully.

A PLA case is bio-based and prints easily but softens around 60 °C — it could deform in a hot car. An ABS case is oil-based but tougher and more heat-resistant. Designers weigh sustainability against in-use performance.
